newsitem.title: USA: CME HOGS, BELLIES END MIXED ON CASH, TECHNICALS.
newsitem.headline: CME HOGS, BELLIES END MIXED ON CASH, TECHNICALS.

text.p: Weak cash markets pressured the spot CME hog contract as technicals supported back months at the close, while the opposite pattern prevailed in pork belly futures, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.675 cent per lb lower to 0.450 higher with August off most at 79.200 and October off 0.125 at 71.925 cents. Pork bellies ended 2.650 higher to 0.900 lower with only August up at 84.850, and February off most at 73.750 cents.
Spot hog futures remained pressured from a weak tone to cash hogs, a lower index and liquidation ahead of its expiration on Thursday, traders said.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.19 at $79.23 per cwt.

However, back months again found technical support and moved up for net gains at times. October held chart support above Tuesday's low of 71.650 cents and moved up for a gain before spillover from August weighed on prices, they said.

E.D.&F. Man bought August late to pare the loss while selling remained scattered. Rand Financials and Rosenthal Collins bought October early and Lind-Waldock sold late. In hog options, ADM Investor Services bought August 79 puts and Refco bought October 68 and 70 puts, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures were the opposite with August rallying on short-covering prompted by apparent bottoming action in the cash market and belief that deliverable stocks were mostly in strong hands, traders said.
Cash bellies were quoted a little firmer at noon from the USDA with 14-16 lb bellies trading at $79 per cwt after ranging as low as $78 on Tuesday.

Back months continued to trade technically with February falling to chart support at 73.000 cents early before recovering. However, prices could still work lower as the trend appears lower, they said.

Saul Stone, E.D.&F. Man and Lind-Waldock sold February early before buying by LFG and ABN Chicogo Corp lent support. E.D.&F. Man sold late while Fimat Futures USA bought. Rand Financials notably bought August late, pit sources said.
